overall: The AG found the Commission violated the OML by discussing legal counsel matters in executive session that did not fit a statutory purpose, and that the executive session notice was insufficiently specific; it ordered compliance and release of minutes.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Commission convened in executive session for an improper purpose by discussing matters with its legal counsel at the December 3, 2024 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: We find here that the Commission’s discussions with legal counsel were not appropriate for executive session.

allegations.summary: The executive session topic on the December 3, 2024 notice cited Purposes 6 and 7 without enough detail, omitting the enabling statute and that minutes would be reviewed.
allegations.key_passage: Moreover, we find that the notice of the December 3, 2024, meeting was insufficiently specific.

allegations.summary: Review of two sets of executive session minutes and discussion of whether those sessions' purposes had concluded, held in executive session under Purpose 7, was addressed.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements.

Within 30 days of the letter, release the executive session minutes of the December 3, 2024 meeting in their entirety, without redaction or withholding, and notify the AG's office that it has done so.
remedy_passage: we order the Commission, within 30 days of the date of this letter, to release the executive session minutes of the meeting held on December 3, 2024, in their entirety and to notify our office that it has done so.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
